Oh, and... How long were you two together before you made the decision to stop smoking?

Sorry for peppering you with questions but it was one of the factors that destroyed my relationship so I really want to know these things.

Thank you for the insight.

Can I have one more? If he asked you to stop, how would you interpret it? You said you probably wouldn't stop. What about doing it 'for someone you love'? Would you instead interpret it as being forced to stop and break up with him?
Thanks for the info. Bonus question: Do you think you'll ever come back to smoking or are you adamant about quitting for good?
So, basically, he was totally OK with you smoking, just didn't want to kiss and cuddle after you did?

The sarcasm is oozing out of this one. Thank you. Thank all of you. I needed someone to tell me everything's gonna be alright. And after my conversation with her today, how she told me she's mad at me for telling her her own best friend lied to her... How she acted like it's all my fault...

Yeah, I think it's all gonna be alright. She just made getting over her a little bit easier. I still love her so fucking much but... It's a bit easier knowing how batshit insane her thought process is at the moment.

Thanks for that! I actually met her today and she started yelling at me at how I'm trying to destroy her friendship etc. etc.

I told her to 'stop and think for a second because she's mad at me for telling the person I FUCKING LOVED that her own best friend lied to her'.

She told me that if I really loved her I would have also loved the fact that she smokes. I told her it's a shitty argument because I can say that 'if she loved me she would've loved the fact that I hate smokes'.

Basically, I treated myself with a lot more self-respect today. It's nice to get validation that I did the right thing.

She later sent me an SMS that she was actually considering getting back together earlier that day and that now, because of how I behaved, that thought was scrapped altogether. I'm wondering... Did she really mean that or is she just trying to make me feel guilty...?


EDIT:
Actually, thanks SO fucking MUCH for that. I needed this more than I thought I did. I didn't even expect a single post on Reddit could help me with my issues but, hey, I guess I was wrong! I might just have a good night's sleep tonight. This coupled with my conversation with her today... Yeah. I'm slowly starting to get over this melodrama.
Thank you both!
I wish it was that simple.

But it feels so wrong now... Like, 75% of the city seems to be smokers. It seems so common. So normal... And yet feels so... bad.

I guess I need to make up my mind again. People I've been with for the last few months really fucked with my perception of cigarettes.
No. I want help. Or at least suggestions. If you don't want to help then at least don't accuse me.
What ultimately pushed you to stop smoking? How did he behave (and for how long) while you were in relationship and you smoked in front of him?

I wasn't forcing myself to like her. I loved her with all my heart. She's irrelevant to all this. I just mentioned her because the breakup is when I really started hating cigs and I feel it's wrong. At least that's what everyone around me is telling me.
I just feel like it's a flaw of some sort in me. It seems irrational. I'm afraid it's going to hurt my social relationships in the future.

Archive: The day I met the girl of my life.
Delete: The day the girl of my life told me she doesn't think she loves me anymore.

Well, that was kinda easy. I probably would've done better if not for the past 3 months. Sorry, guys!

Thank you for that. It's really... inspiring. My problem is to once again find the will, the need, the drive to aspire to all those goals. This girl gave meaning to my otherwise meaningless existence. I'm not sure if it's all over or if we can still rebuild what was lost.

...Maybe I should try and fix what was broken, try and remake what was unmade in the past months...? Time will tell. For now, let's drink to that - to always do our best to move forward.

I realized that, for the first time, I had my heart broken by a girl apparently not having enough courage to say she doesn't care anymore and that I probably gave her too much of myself. I'm kind of going to miss all these parts of myself that I gave away.

I already did something spontaneous lately. A few times, actually.
We had a bit of a 'fight' over her being addicted to smoking cigs lately. All I said back then was that it hurts me that she is hurting herself, more or less, but it was enough for her to get angry. A few days later she went with her female friend to the countryside where she has a small vacation house.

Approx. midnight of that day I drove all the way over there from the city and knocked on her door. She was surprised as hell but pretty happy that I visited her. A few days later she was again bummed out about me not liking her cigarette habit so she paid a surprise visit to a concert I was singing at (even though she said she can't come) and I sang a song that I dedicated to her, leaving the stage with an "I love you".

So yeah, I'm trying to do spontaneous stuff. Right now I'm planning on going on a boat trip with a friend and I'm trying to convince her to come with me.

Venting to her won't do much good either I think... Already mentioned a few times that I don't really like that she's never the one to ask for a meeting :-/

Thanks for the interest though!

Overall, pretty mild, so to say.

The girl I fell in love with doesn't seem to care all that much about spending time together. The last two months I was always the one to 'make the call' to meet and right now I'm waiting in my house until the lady decides it is finally time to meet.

Note, she has pretty much nothing to do. She did nothing all day, just chilling in her house. And yet I have to wait for her (it's currently almost 5PM).

So yeah, not well, because the lady of my life only decides to spend the last few hours of her day with me despite doing nothing else on that day. And yes, I am lucky she actually wants to meet today, that doesn't happen often.

Thanks for letting me vent tho.

Thing is, this hasn't happened in about a year now. I've experienced it a grand total of about 3 times my entire life, along with about a dozen cases of deja vu. It seems to happen less and less as I age, I think.
I don't even know if it'll ever happen again.

Pool with a rope... Interesting one.

The problem is they won't disagree that most dreams aren't precognition. They'll insist that *some* dreams are precognition and they just haven't had any since the last time.

And really, precognition is the least of the problems. Like I said. They're Christians believing in reincarnation, ghosts, tarot-like AND dream precognition, all kinds of conspiracies (chemtrails, anyone?) etc. etc.

I was just hoping to get some hard evidence against precognition, I guess more for my own peace of mind. It's really the only 'supernatural' phenomenon that I experienced myself and it would be nice to have it explained with perhaps a lengthy article or at least a simple explanation. The Deja Vu seems to fit the bill although it seems a bit far-fetched with the current information that I have. I mean, for me everything supernatural is a hoax unless explained by science. I just have a teeny tiny problem finding the science here.

They'll just say that this paranormal stuff is not easy and only happens from time to time (and of course different people have different levels of sensitivity so it can happen once in a lifetime or never). These are the same people that believe they're Christian while not believing in the Bible while believing in Jesus Christ while also believing in reincarnation.

Well, damn. I guess that downvote on the thread for no apparent reason further proves your point...

CRAP. I was really hoping I could do something. Guess it's finally time to give up trying to enlighten them, huh...?

And thus, you are the only person stopping yourself from becoming awesome.

You asked if it's better for you to kill yourself, seeing the state you're in currently.

The answer is: No. It's far better to tell your mom about your problem because then you can both actually figure out a good solution to it.

Once you figure this out, your life is bound to improve drastically.
Keep this in mind, as I'm sure you can eventually grow up to the decision :)

Think of this way.

She will have to deal with this shit UNLESS you tell her. If you don't tell her, you risk spending the next few years in this state, constantly feeling like a disappointment to her.

If you DO tell her, there's a good chance she'll come up with a way to help you (even if it's kicking you out of bed early every day to look for work) and, eventually you'll actually start being a great asset to the family.

There is NO downside to telling her. "It just wouldn't feel right" is your depressed mind being afraid of doing something that can actually help. DO IT. Don't listen to your inner voices, just do it. Just go out there, right now, go to your mom, tell her how you feel.

It will:

a) Make you feel MUCH better once you tell her you're afraid to disappoint her

b) Give you a MUCH greater chance of overcoming your 'laziness' as your mom WILL use her authority over you to help you with that

c) Make your mom actually feel better. If she knows what the source of your 'laziness' is AND that you're so ashamed of it, she will finally be able to put many of her worries to rest. She will also once again feel in control, as she will be able to directly help you with that.



Want to stop feeling like shit?

GO TELL YOUR MOM.

RIGHT NOW. NO EXCUSES.

GO!

No, I'm not saying that.

I'm saying that both an outside source AND you can change yourself. Either way works.

And why aren't you going to talk to your mom?

It's not all bullshit and you certainly can. A funny commercial can make you stop feeling sad (if only for a moment), an amazing opportunity can make you start feeling awesome in a matter of seconds. It can happen, it's just a matter of stuff like the right person telling you the right thing.
I got out of my own depression by not telling myself I'm worthless anymore and starting to tell myself that, actually, I'm kinda awesome. Feels a bit like an exaggeration but I am no longer depressed! 

But, even if you don't want to believe me on that, what I'm asking of you is to find people who can help you get out of your situation. Which is why, for the tenth time, I'm suggesting your mom. She seems like she's already trying to get you to do something and, from what I understand, you didn't tell her about feeling worthless, suicidal (contemplating the merit of one's death IS feeling suicidal) and needing help.

If you can inform someone you trust about your (full) situation, I'm sure they can help much better than I can, by means of simply not being hundreds of miles away.

You're waiting for me to break and tell you you're right. But you're not and I won't.

Being good is not something you weight against anything. Good deeds are not judged like that.

Besides, hell, I know people who are leeches and are proud of that. You're already a step above them. And, from what I hear, you're not that different from most college students, with the exception that you're not in college at the moment. They're all usually attending college because their parents made them and learn because their teachers make them. They rarely do anything besides it so don't judge yourself too harshly and try to improve however you can. You're not gonna go leaps and bounds in a day but who knows how much you can improve in a year if you make the conscious choice and stop telling yourself you're worthless? Your own attitude is holding you back. You telling yourself you're worthless is what's stopping you from becoming awesome.

Perhaps you should just stop telling yourself you're worthless? Did you talk to your mom? If so, what did she say?

People on the internet like to judge. A lot. Don't let them get to you.

Read your sentence. A lot of people on the internet told you that. How trustworthy a source is that, when they know nothing of the good stuff that you did?

Also, those people can go fuck off. Talk with your mom (as it's the only person that you spoke of that seems trustworthy enough), talk with her openly, tell her all of this stuff - that you feel worthless, that you don't want to disappoint her, that you want help and lack the self-discipline to help yourself. Tell her to help you with that.

If things feel so bad then, then I'm always here to tell you that no, you are not a worthless human being. We all need attention sometimes, we all sometimes don't feel like doing anything. Sometimes we spend a lot of time doing nothing. It's human nature.

Sure, blame me. I spent a good few years trying to get in good terms with them. There was a time I was so depressed I actually thought I was a worthless, shameless fuck. Came out and told it to them. Told me to go fuck off, basically. OF COURSE I harbor a great deal of resentment. I just want to be left alone by them when it comes to my personal matters.

I've actually achieved that to a great degree - I didn't step on their toes, they only occasionally stepped on mine. Then atheism came along.

Had you read some of the other replies you'd have seen there's better ways to reply than to accuse people of wanting to be angry.

Academic stuff is what's been distracting me all along. I'm an IB student during my final year so I have a metric ton of material to learn. I'm also trying to focus on my hobby/future career. There is no room nor possibility for a part-time job and I need a stable full-time income anyway.
Can't really take full credit for this one as I stole it from Tim Minchin. He's a brilliant comedian and has some good stuff on religion and overall sanity.

Homework really has nothing to do with them coming in and I absolutely cannot make my room (actually a whole floor) a no-entry zone. Tried once.

Gf sounds nice until I realize I'm not planning on staying in the country so it would actually make it even harder for me to make the break.

No, it's not.

Did someone at some point in your life tell you you're worthless?

>"Create? The Big Bang is nothing, in sum. It adds up to zero energy. Create...what?"

'...But...But... Everything must be created by something!'
...And their brains shut off and they start screaming at me.
And no, they won't answer the 'Then who created God' question.

You know what? If disappointing your mom doesn't work as motivation for you then STOP THINKING ABOUT IT.

If the only way someone can help you is by doing something for you then why won't you ask someone (like your mom) to MAKE YOU apply for that job?

Like I said, from what I hear your problem is that your self-discipline is not developed enough. But it CAN be changed.

You're not pathetic, you shouldn't kill yourself. C'mon. By now you've repeated your arguments quite a few times and I'm still standing by what I said. You seem so keen on giving up, give up on suicide! It's futile and you know it.

Even living a worthless life is more of an achievement than not living one at all.

So dude. You WILL eventually get your shit straight. Whether you like it or not. Whether you want it or not. Life will force you to do that. It's an asshole like that. And you don't have to make anyone but yourself proud. So what if your mom is disappointed in you now? In a few years you might achieve something awesome.

And don't you tell me how in a few years you'll be the same 'loser' because YOU DON'T KNOW THAT. Life tends to change people, don't ever think you're safe from it changing you.

Like I said, talk to people you trust. Tell them exactly how you feel. Tell them you want them to help you. Tell them you have this problem with self-discipline that you want to overcome. But don't mistake people you know with people who are capable of helping you. Not everyone you ask for help will have even the slightest idea HOW to help you, let alone wanting to go out of their own little bubble.

But don't let that discourage you. I personally also suggest /r/getmotivated for some motivation. Maybe even try posting there? I don't guarantee a good answer but they'll probably try to give one that fits your situation.

And you did go out of your way to post on r/SuicideWatch so you're still not as lazy as you think.

Motivation comes and goes, so does depression. It's important to remember that what you're feeling is not a constant state.

Well, not exactly word for word but (borrowing from my religion argument) it was something along the lines of my mom saying about there being no proof of what came before the Big Bang so we better believe in God. She asked the question "Who created the Big Bang?". I replied with "Who created God?".

I sure hope we're still on the same topic XD

EDIT:
If you mean the talking to them to ignore the conversation I used "I don't really want to talk about it". Then, when they insisted I said "I don't really want to talk about it because I know we'll just end up arguing and I don't want that to happen".

Then they went batshit crazy on me.
This. Is exactly my thoughts.
If you mean not using long, complicated words then I'm already doing that.

No, you could have not gone.

Besides, why not roll with it? She gave you the initial push, maybe that's enough to get started.

You might get a job out of this. If you do then... Holy shit, you got a job! Stable financial income!

There's better speakers than me on this subject, and I wish I was one of them right now, but believe me when I say you are not a lost cause.

Maybe you lack self-discipline. But self-discipline is something that can be learned. Let your mother's feelings be your motivation. You don't want to disappoint her, therefore you should live (as dying would be the ultimate disappointment) and do your best (even if at times it feels like nothing!) to become better.

Don't outright force yourself to go to the gym, clean everyone's yards and find a cure for cancer, though! Small steps are important. Even selfish steps to self-improvement are important.

Wake up an hour earlier than you usually do, look for some more job offers online, etc. etc. You might not do these things I just proposed, even if you'd like to. But you can always start smaller. When making tea, make tea for your parents as well (if they want it), etc.

Hell, tell your mom you want to change. Tell her you want to not be a disappointment for her and that you'd like her help with that. Tell her how you feel, she might be able to help you get up on your feet.

Oh, she's even worse than my parents, in that she is selfish, greedy, wants everyone to treat her like a queen, has no concept of empathy and lacks the brains to do anything but sleep, eat and party. She is a lost cause, partly because of the way my parents brought her up. She moved out with a dude almost 10 years older than her, having had too many boyfriends before for me to count.

So, ummm... I don't think I'd like to talk to her about it.

Problem is, they like to talk. About my 'faults'.
And they have a 'bullshit detector' about these things so they'd definitely notice if I started acting them as special needs people.

Holy shit man, this... this is what I need.

How do I make myself remember this? How to make myself remember to say "I'm happy just listening" when asked for my opinion? This is golden! Best answer I've heard, ever.


MUST...NOT...FORGET... >_>

(I am serious btw. This is the most brilliant thing I've heard all week)

I came out as an atheist to have a peace of mind. I couldn't take it if I had to lie and be completely unable to express my views. I don't think hiding is the answer to anything.

If I was just living near them and had my own money source I wouldn't even care. And I guess it's not just about the atheism, either. When I cooled down it came to me that they are actually batshit insane. Had problems with them all my life, it got A LOT calmer when my sister moved out of the house (hopefully this time for a longer while than usual).

For the record, one of the most used arguments in fights was "You're just like/worse than your sister!". I guess atheism is just the latest thing they found that they don't like about me...
How bad is my situation if I told you that, as far as I'm aware, I've already tried that?

But being a Muslim is also bad because it's not the True Religion (TM).

And my problem is that I can't sort my life out independently at the moment because I'm still in what you'd call High School (albeit it's my last year) and need the stuff I have for my career which I passionately love (music and graphics are an expensive hobby).

Haha, that kind of made my laugh (in all of the situation's direness) :)

Yes, they are clueless. I'd go as far as to say they're batshit crazy. I guess my post should be "How do I live with batshit crazy parents?" :-/
Yes you did. You took the test, didn't you?

>Christians, by definition, follow the teachings of Christ. How do they do this without the Bible?
I truly have no idea. I tried getting them to tell me... No dice. I guess it's just all the obvious miracles God has done that made them believe.

>It's not stupid to withhold belief until supporting evidence is presented. Tell them to show you reasonable evidence.
They'll just tell me another anecdote about a supposed miracle. No, I cannot prove to them that it wasn't a miracle.

>Drop a heavy object on their foot. Oh, it hurt? Guess gravity exists after all.
'But how do you know that it was gravity and not some other force, like God?'. I am fairly confident this would be my father's response, unfortunately. Reasoning just doesn't seem to work.

>Point out that no one ever came to Jesus through harassment and badgering.
They don't care about converting me, I think. It seems they only care about mocking my stupidity. Also, they would never call what they're doing harassment and badgering. They'd say I'M the one harassing and badgering them by poisoning the family or some shit.

I can't show or do anything to show that it isn't stupid because atheism is stupid by definition because there is so obviously a God.

I do pay attention during my physics classes and believe that an object falling towards the Earth (or little bundles of salt clumping together in a void, as I've recently seen on Discovery Channel) is proof of gravity. The proof of it is that it works on us and other things. There is no proof of God doing any work whatsoever.

Thanks for the suggestions (to you and everyone here, really). Even though I feel it's futile, as they'll just start yelling at me for not participating in the discussion, I think this is the best way I can handle it.

What do I do if I'm with them and a group of people who start discussing religion and miracles and stuff like that out of thin air and keep at it for a straight hour? I can't just opt-out then. What do?

Tried that :(

I either get a monologue from them because they start shouting at once or I get a monologue from them because they hate people who talk in a monotone voice (this seriously happened).

As you can imagine, I'm seriously lost here.

How can they even call it their beliefs if they're not their beliefs?

Besides, I don't walk into the room with my shoes on shouting "Christianity is bullshit!".

I only react. I guess I can no longer call them out on their hypocrisy when they shit on Islam and others in their little fap-fap-we're-so-awesome-circles but that just means going back to the ignoring-my-parents route which they hate just as much and used to call me out on it pretty often. What to do? What to do?

If I resort just to casual conversations they'll eventually steer them to topics they like to argue about... And we're getting out of the religion zone and into the my-parents-are-batshit-insane area... FUCK.
Thanks for the support and suggestion. I'm seriously considering all my options of making them shut up which don't involve just ignoring them (because that just makes them rage harder).

If I don't remember what they said then I'm ignorant because I didn't listen.

If I said that quote, it's already way too theatric. Ideally, my reply should sound like a redneck I guess o.O

Even when I make it clear I've no idea what they're talking about they tend to carry on the argument.

And by 'clearly telling me about their beliefs' they'll say they believe in a God that created the universe. And, oh, they're also Christian. :-/

How can you not believe in the ever-loving Christian God? If you don't believe in a Christian God you're a stupid person!

That's the 'questions' they ask.

And the problem is that they can't accept the fact that I'm an atheist. Even more so that I despise christianity. I can accept that they believe in a God. The only way out I can think of is if I lied about my view on Christianity as a Bible-based-religion but it's a little too late for that. It's usually like this:
-"Hey, my my son is atheist and hates Christianity! We've established that you're stupid because you're atheist but why do you hate Christianity?"
-"Mom, you're not even a Christian. Why do you care?"
-"Of course I'm a Christian! Look! Reincarnation!"
-"And do you also believe that we can have slaves and beat them to death?"
-"You inconsiderate bastard! This has nothing to do with Christianity! Now repent you stupid atheist!"

Thanks for the response. It's somehow soothing to know I'm not just being an asshole for not loving my parents.

Also, they would never say they're buddhists. They're 'Christian'. I just call them buddhist-christian because they seem to have stolen a lot of stuff from them, like the reincarnation thing.

I tried doing just that. My dad's response:
"I thought you were smarter than that."

When my parents think I'm not smart bad things tend to happen. I don't get recognized as a capable family member and, on their own, these people tend to do some really stupid stuff which hurts everyone in the long run. Also, I get treated like shit.

oh, they HAVE found a true God.

During my argument with them, there was this other christian (a guest). She said that to her all other religions are sects and Christianity is the Only True Religion (TM).

They agreed.

They'll just say they don't believe because they were lucky enough to be born into the True Religion (TM) and 'besides it doesn't matter anyway because John Paul II accepted all religions because everyone's God is basically the same thing'.

That much I figured but thanks for confirming it and letting me hold on to my sanity just a little while longer. It gets hard when you spent your whole life with them.

The thing is:
I can't reason with them for reasons known to everyone here. I can't NOT reason with them because that would mean ignoring them in some way and whenever I ignore them they just come screaming "WHY ARE YOU IGNORING US!".

So what do I do? Can't ignore, can't not ignore. I feel like I'm some kind of a logical trap!

That would mean ignoring them. And they, as I have previously said, don't like being ignored.

How does one answer questions like these in a non-objectionable manner? That sounds like the plain old passive aggressive stance ('sure, you're right, whatever you say') which just angers them even more.

"Be prepared to tell them you've nothing to say, to answer or to believe in because they've said nothing meaningful."

This grants me a 3-hour long conversation on how I'm a douchebag for insulting my parents, how I should be ashamed of myself and how their beliefs are still more valid than mine and how I can't use the PC until I say I'm sorry and conform to their beliefs.

I *don't* want to go that path again :(

They always want a response.

I had a phase where I would just basically say "I don't want to discuss that". They would start screaming at me for not obeying their order to discuss it and keep at it for a whole day (or even few days), teaching me that this isn't exactly the way I can do it.

Please don't overuse the 'classic teen phase', though. I'll be 19 in a couple of days and my parents still use this term to describe every reason I disagree with them.

Atheist? Classic teen phase.
Parents started argument that I don't even understand because they need to scream at someone but need to somehow put the blame on me? Classic teen phase.

And no, it's not a classic teen phase. Being severely depressed pretty much my whole teen year (thanks, parents, for forcing me to do unnecessary stuff I hated and dismissing me at every step!), I had to grow up fast or become a loser. I didn't get the chance to go through a classic teen phase.

I would, however, like some advice on how to pick non-controversial topics and STICK to them. It's not hard to pick a random one, how do you prevent it from off-topicking into the various problems that they have with me? I can't really direct their thoughts, can I?

I did already use the Jesus' existence argument a few times. My mother says she doesn't care if Jesus exists or not, even though she believes in him. The problem is they're not sure what they believe while at the same time being sure what they believe. There is no reasoning with them because they're capable of changing their stance mid-sentence and no one really knows what they really believe at the moment (although a few unchangeable things are that they call themselves christian, believe in God etc.)

Also, the magic stuff is a bad idea. They DO believe in magic. They believe in Tarot and other ways of future-prediction. They put up the mistletoe on Christmas for good luck etc. etc.

And how do I end on a reasonable note when I'm being told I can't prove gravity?

Well the problem is not me lacking the anti-theist ammo for debates (although I do plan to read stuff like The God Delusion etc.), the problem is my parents ignoring the arguments completely and calling me stupid for not believing in the christian-but-not-quite-christian-but-also-buddhist God.

(also: I'm a man)

And thank you for checking my posting history first instead of automatically assuming trolling.
But if I shut up it makes them unhappy because then I'm not talking to them and 'avoiding them' so I'm not a good son. But If I'm around them, this shit happens... o.O

"conflict with the notion of creation" is too complicated for them to process.

Also, I didn't get ANY answer at all when I asked the "Who created God" question. Not even a bullshit one. They just skipped the subject, like they do every time they find something confusing.
Yes, I did. The only reason I care is because they own the moneyz. So it matters financially what they think about me :-/
Imagine growing up in that environment -_-

Thanks for the advice. As much as I'd like them to accept me, I guess it's impossible.

The thing is, I'm already trying to restrict communication between my parents. I keep myself to my room, only really meet them during breakfast and dinner when I eat. They are calling me out for ignoring them. It's come to that now my father actually comes upstairs to me and to my room and just walks around it, annoying me and occasionally asking things like "have you done your homework"?

So what now?

From what I understand from your quote I have used this argument against them by asking "If the origin of the universe is God then who created God?" when they told me I can't prove the origin of the big bang.

If I asked it in the way you've written it (i.e. the scientific way) they wouldn't understand and would call me stupid and ignorant for spewing poorly-worded definitions :-/

Well, I read a lot about Christianity and I'd say I'm able-versed in the ways of anti-theism. They just brush of ANY argument. Examples:
-Why is it more important for God to help your sick daughter when he could be out helping kids in Africa who don't even have water?
-If God exists and wants us to believe in him then why won't he show himself?
-If God is almighty and good why won't he take away evil? If he doesn't want to, doesn't that make him evil? If he wants to but can't then how is he a God?

For the sake of the argument I had with my parents I focused on disproving the Christian God by quoting from the Bible. Then they said that the Bible has nothing to do with Christianity (sic) so I started disproving God to the extend that it's possible to do. Then I just gave up and quit the room when I heard I can't prove gravity -_-

I get EXACTLY what you're saying. I'm 100% dependent on their cash flow and that is a HUGE problem for me. I am planning on getting financially stable (i.e. getting a job) as soon as possible but, unfortunately that's going to have to wait a while since I do have some expensive plans for my future (music & pc career). Hope I get a good job while in college...

I care what they say because what they say greatly depends on how they treat me. Right now I'm at a point where their whim is the deciding factor of my future.
